helpful: LIFT then FIRE cue clarified release requirement
Coil OFF states and objective transitions
Route and approach labels consistently enabled progress
friction: First patrol burst left target alive; combination of aiming and movement needed correction.
Threat and interaction overlays compete for scene area.
uncertainties: Terminal critical elimination is not assigned to a particular shot by this reviewer.
No claim that DASH prevented damage; terminal phase evade count is zero.

limitations: Synthetic paused Chromium touch emulation and software WebGL; no physical device certification.
Captures release contacts and pause; approximately 3s live or 1.2s FIRE boundaries shortened waits; no human reaction-time or causal quality benefit inferred.
Continuous held-burst rearming comfort not established, including captureHeld.
Physical phones, Safari, audio, hardware performance and continuous enjoyment unassessed.
learningForAttempt2: Route/approach and coil selectors were legible and effective; patrol tap/drag aiming remained uncertain. Will preserve failures and use fresh views for corrections.

assessment.scale: 0 unusable in observed scope; 5 playable with substantial friction; 7 good with noticeable friction; 9 excellent with minor friction; 10 exceptional across assessed scope. Holistic judgment, not a win/loss grade or arithmetic average.

reasons.overallMobile: A coherent, atmospheric short mission with clear assisted progression, readable key controls and satisfying visible objective completion. Manual patrol aim/drag needed repeated correction and firing/cover feedback was initially hard to interpret. Both completions used substantial route, approach and shot assists; those wins do not certify unassisted combat quality.
reasons.controls: MOVE and FIRE worked together; turns, DASH cooldown and zoom were observable. Patrol aiming missed or failed to finish targets and first-run corrections were awkward. Coil selectors were effective. Continuous held-burst comfort remains unassessed.
reasons.gameplay: Recoveries, changing Custodian states, coil disabling and deck upload gave a complete objective arc. Visible danger and reload added demands, though route assistance carried much navigation and enemies could be left behind. Unassisted balance and broader content unassessed.
reasons.presentation: Distinct rainy teal industrial setting, reflective ground, large typography and consistent terminal treatment. Strong visual identity in software rendering; audio unassessed.
reasons.usability: HOLD ROUTE / HOLD APPROACH, explicit coil selectors, automatic reload and detailed assist accounting reduced uncertainty. Firing rearm/cover behavior and simultaneous threat overlays took learning. No menu/settings exploration beyond the visible opening screen.
reasons.readability: Main objective, ammo, health and touch controls legible at 844x390. World text and tiny distant enemies required attention; threat/interaction panels occupied useful scene space.

protocol.input: JSON-lines native two-contact touchscreen acts only
protocol.screenshots: Every returned screenshot viewed before adaptive continuation, separate image calls. One new scene target coordinate per batch; anchored FIRE could follow.
protocol.waits: All waits <=3000ms; helper boundaries inspected. FIRE-limited a1-patrol-manual wait shortened from 1100 to about 1057ms; route waits typically shortened to approximately 2980ms. No skipped-step assumption or bypass.
protocol.aimPause: After zoomed first-run capture, resumed empty act and inspected fresh unzoom view before scene target. Second-run zoom followed by anchored route input and fresh view before new scene target.
